title: Yann LeCun on AI risk, effective altruism, Dario Amodei and building AMI Labs
key_facts: LeCun told Fortune (interview by Emily Forlini) he does not worry 'at all' about AI wiping out humanity.
He has 'zero concerns' about the recent rogue AI incidents, including the July Hugging Face hack by OpenAI's agents, which he called 'totally preventable'.
He called effective altruism 'super toxic' and called Amodei 'deluded' and 'crazy'.
He worries more about regulatory capture than extinction and said Amodei is 'honest' but doing what is best for Anthropic as it nears an IPO.
LeCun left Meta after 12 years to found AMI Labs, based in Paris with 60+ staff, building world models on the JEPA architecture.
AMI's first product is coming 'soon' and may involve open models.
quote_evidence: Those agents are doing exactly what they've been asked to do.
why_it_matters_hint: A top AI researcher publicly disputes the extinction-risk case behind calls for regulation.
notes: Interview itself not read; The Next Web summary used.
